lanchuan-a01.title: The Ferryman's Old Umbrella
lanchuan-a01.brief: Under the eaves of the old thatched hut at Tidewatch Ferry, an oiled-paper umbrella with two broken bamboo ribs hangs tilted year-round, its handle bearing a faint, carved character "Qing". If curious wayfarers ask about it, Song Laolu merely taps his tobacco pipe against a wooden piling: "It's hung there for nineteen years. lanchuan-q01.title: Severed Palms: The Broken Eighteen Dragon-Subduing Palms and the Sealed Stances Case
lanchuan-q01.brief: The Eighteen Dragon-Subduing Palms, the supreme martial art of the Beggars' Sect—the realm's greatest faction—has only been passed down through its first twelve stances across generations in the Lanchuan martial world. Where the final six stances vanished remains a subject of endless dispute. Some claim they were lost during the Song-Jin wars; others say their unyielding fury defied heaven and invited divine retribution; still, old beggars mutter in drunken stupors that the old sect master himself swore an oath and sealed them away in the deep mountains.

objectives.lanchuan-q01.stage4: Niu Bushi's Breakdown: If presented with the clay bowl and the manuscript, stubborn Elder Niu breaks down in tears, revealing three loose pages of remnant mental methods (I43) kept because "the old sect master wished to protect future generations from being consumed by demonic force."
objectives.lanchuan-q01.stage5: Trial of Heart with the Ravine Woodcutter: Bring the rubbing, old bowl, and manuscript to meet Old Woodcutter Tao. The old man sighs deeply, finally tracing out the true energetic pivots of the final six stances on the sand.
objectives.lanchuan-q01.ending: Decide how to conclude this affair.

lanchuan-q02.title: "Tale of the Seven Friends" — The Double Ninth Night Nineteen Years Ago and the Sunken Ship Chang Geng
lanchuan-q02.brief: Nineteen years ago (the fourth year of Ninghe), on the night of the Double Ninth Festival (the ninth day of the ninth lunar month), an earth-shattering tragedy struck Mist-Wave Manor in the heart of Qingping Lake. The "Seven Friends of Lanchuan," who once shared deep bonds and took martial oaths as sworn brothers, shattered and went their separate ways that very night. One perished in a sea of flames, while the rest scattered into the miasmal wastes of the northern frontiers; for twenty years, none have dared speak a single word of those events in front of others.

lanchuan-q03.title: "Lantern of the Returning Sail" — Lighting a Lamp for Yourself in the Humble Jianghu
lanchuan-q03.brief: Wandering through the jianghu for decades, where does my soul find rest? No matter how illustrious the disciples of renowned sects become, what they strive for is but the pedigree of masters and elders. A true warrior must ultimately carve out a sanctuary in the mud-and-water market towns across the land—a place to shelter from wind and rain, where destitute brothers can step inside to drink a bowl of hot soup. A single roof, a bond of good faith, and a family craft make for an ever-burning "Lantern of the Returning Sail."
